provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Health and hygiene
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state personal cleanliness routines.
The pupils should be able to explain how germs spread.

Introduction:
Today we will learn about keeping our bodies clean. We already know that dirty hands can make us sick.

Content:
Personal cleanliness means keeping your body and surroundings clean. We wash our hands with soap and water before eating. We brush our teeth every morning. We bathe daily to remove dirt from our skin. Germs are tiny living things that can make us ill. We prevent germs by not sharing our personal items like toothbrushes. We cover our mouth when we cough or sneeze to stop germs from spreading.

Class activity:
Pupils will wash their hands properly following the teacher's demonstration.

Evaluation questions:
1. What do we use to wash our hands?
2. Name two ways to prevent germs.
3. Why should we not share our toothbrushes?

Summary:
Keeping our bodies clean helps us stay healthy and prevent sickness.

topics.title: Food and nutrition
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list the classes of food.
The pupils should be able to identify a balanced meal.

Introduction:
We eat food every day to grow strong. Today we will learn about different types of food.

Content:
Food gives us energy to play and learn. There are classes of food: carbohydrates like rice and yam give us energy. Proteins like beans and fish help us grow. Fruits and vegetables give us vitamins. We need a balanced meal with all classes of food to stay healthy. A balanced meal has food from all groups like rice, fish, beans and plantain.

Class activity:
Pupils will draw a balanced meal plate with food from different classes.

Evaluation questions:
1. Name one food rich in carbohydrates.
2. What does protein do for our body?
3. Which class of food gives us vitamins?
4. Draw a balanced meal plate.

Summary:
Eating different types of food helps our body grow strong and stay healthy.

topics.title: The environment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain why we keep the environment clean.
The pupils should be able to identify different types of waste.

Introduction:
Our environment is where we live, work and play. We must keep it clean to stay healthy.

Content:
Keeping the environment clean means removing dirt and waste from our surroundings. We have different types of waste: paper waste like old newspapers, plastic waste like water bottles, and food waste like plantain peels. We use bins to collect waste. We should not throw rubbish on the ground. Dirty environment can make us sick with diseases like malaria.

Class activity:
Pupils will sort different types of waste into correct bins.

Evaluation questions:
1. Why do we keep our environment clean?
2. Name three types of waste.
3. What do we use to collect waste?
4. What disease can dirty environment cause?

Summary:
A clean environment helps us stay healthy and live well.

topics.title: Weather
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify weather symbols.
The pupils should be able to record daily weather.

Introduction:
The weather changes every day. We can know the weather by looking at the sky.

Content:
Weather is the state of the air outside. We have different weather types: sunny, rainy, cloudy and windy. Weather symbols are pictures that show the weather. A sun symbol means it is sunny. A cloud with raindrops means it will rain. We can make a weather chart to record the weather each day. In harmattan season, the weather is dry and dusty.

Class activity:
Pupils will draw weather symbols and complete a simple weather chart for the week.

Evaluation questions:
1. What does a sun symbol mean?
2. Name two types of weather.
3. What season is dry and dusty in Nigeria?
4. Draw a rainy weather symbol.

Summary:
Weather symbols help us know what kind of day to expect.

topics.title: Energy: sun, heat and light
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list sources of heat and light.
The pupils should be able to explain sun safety.

Introduction:
The sun gives us light and heat. Other things can also give us heat and light.

Content:
Heat and light are forms of energy. The sun is our main source of heat and light. Other sources include fire from a kerosene stove, electric bulb and candle. Heat makes things warm. Light helps us see in the dark. We must be safe in the sun. We should not look directly at the sun. We wear hats to protect our heads from the sun.

Class activity:
Pupils will identify sources of heat and light in the classroom.

Evaluation questions:
1. Name two sources of heat.
2. What does light help us do?
3. How can we protect ourselves from the sun?
4. What does a kerosene stove give us?

Summary:
Heat and light are important forms of energy from different sources.

topics.title: Sound energy
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain how sound is made.
The pupils should be able to differentiate between loud and soft sounds.

Introduction:
We hear sounds every day like the school bell and people talking. Today we will learn how sound is made.

Content:
Sound is made when something vibrates or shakes. When we talk, our voice box vibrates. When a drum is hit, the skin vibrates and makes sound. Sound can be loud like a danfo horn or soft like a whisper. Loud sounds can hurt our ears. Soft sounds are gentle on our ears.

Class activity:
Pupils will make different sounds by clapping, whispering and tapping desks.

Evaluation questions:
1. How is sound made?
2. Give an example of a loud sound.
3. Give an example of a soft sound.
4. What vibrates when we talk?

Summary:
Sound is made by vibrations and can be loud or soft.

topics.title: Movement and force
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate push and pull.
The pupils should be able to identify forces around us.

Introduction:
Things move when we use force. We use force every day without realizing it.

Content:
Force is a push or a pull. When we push a door, it opens. When we pull a chair, it moves towards us. Forces can make things move faster, slower, stop or change direction. We use force when we kick a football. We use force when we carry a bucket of water. Gravity is a force that pulls things down to the ground.

Class activity:
Pupils will push and pull objects in the classroom and describe what happens.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is force?
2. Give an example of pushing.
3. Give an example of pulling.
4. What force pulls things to the ground?

Summary:
Force makes things move and can be a push or a pull.

topics.title: Materials
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify different materials.
The pupils should be able to sort materials into groups.

Introduction:
Objects around us are made of different materials. We can group materials by their properties.

Content:
Materials are what things are made of. Wood comes from trees. Metal is hard and strong. Plastic can be many colors. Fabric is soft and used for clothes. Materials have different properties: wood can burn, metal conducts heat, plastic is waterproof. We sort materials based on what they are made of and their properties.

Class activity:
Pupils will sort objects into wood, metal, plastic and fabric groups.

Evaluation questions:
1. Name four materials.
2. What is wood used for?
3. Which material is waterproof?
4. How do we sort materials?

Summary:
Objects are made of different materials with special properties.

topics.title: Technology: tools
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate safe use of simple tools.
The pupils should be able to make a simple craft.

Introduction:
Tools help us do work easily. We must learn to use tools safely.

Content:
Tools are objects that help us work. Simple tools include hammer, scissors, ruler and glue. We use tools to make things easier. When using tools, we must be careful. We hold scissors with the blades pointing away. We wear gloves when using sharp tools. We should not run with tools in our hands.

Class activity:
Pupils will make a simple craft using safe tools like scissors and glue.

Evaluation questions:
1. Name two simple tools.
2. How should we hold scissors?
3. Why do we wear gloves with sharp tools?
4. What should we not do with tools in our hands?

Summary:
Tools help us work but we must use them carefully to stay safe.

topics.title: Revision and project
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recall term's topics.
The pupils should be able to present their project.

Introduction:
Today we will remember what we learned this term and show our projects.

Content:
This term we learned about health and hygiene, food and nutrition, environment, weather, energy, sound, movement, materials and tools. We made projects like weather charts and crafts. Projects help us practice what we learned. We should speak clearly when showing our project to the class.

Class activity:
Pupils will present their term project to the class.

Evaluation questions:
1. Name one thing we learned about health.
2. What is a balanced meal?
3. How is sound made?
4. Show your project to the class.

Summary:
We have learned many things this term and our projects show what we know.
